faq.a: No. You can walk in {{ hours_phrase }}. If you book a visit, we can set time aside for you.

faq.q: Can I keep my number if I switch providers?
faq.a: Yes. In Canada you can keep your number when you change providers. Bring photo ID and your current account number, and don't cancel your old plan first: moving your number ends that service for you.

faq.q: Is T Wireless a Bell store?
faq.a: We're a Bell Authorised Retailer. We sell Bell, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile plans and phones, and Bell internet, TV and home phone.

faq.q: Can you fix my phone or tablet?
faq.a: We repair screens, batteries, charging ports, cameras and more. Tell us your model and the problem, and we'll quote the repair before we start.
Yes. The store has a wheelchair-accessible entrance.

unconfirmed: Postal code: the site shows L6X 0G3 (business card and Google listing); Bell's store locator shows L6X 5K7.

Opening hours: the brief, the site and Bell's store locator say open every day, 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. The Google listing, read on October 27, 2026, shows Sunday 10:30 a.m. to 7 p.m.; one reading of it also showed Monday closed, which a second reading did not reproduce (it showed 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.). The open/closed signs know nothing about holidays, so each Visit page says to phone first on a public holiday, in its own words; keep that line or give real holiday hours.
Example offers: the five offers are examples with $XX prices; replace them with real offers or delete them (build.py --release refuses to build while they remain).
Web address: confirm the site will live at https://www.twireless.ca (site.base_url drives canonical links, the sitemap and the social preview image).

What the store can set up: plans and phones from all three of Bell, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile, Bell internet, Fibe TV, Satellite TV and Home Phone, Bell business plans, Bell SmartPay and the Device Return Option. The brief and the business card say so; check it against the dealer agreement.
Repairs: confirm the repair list each design shows (screens, batteries, charging faults, cameras, speakers and microphones, water damage) and that repairs are quoted before work starts.
Wheelchair access: the entrance is wheelchair accessible (taken from the Google listing); it appears on Home, Visit us and in the FAQ.
Map and directions: the map sketch, and the line "South side of Bovaird, just east of Chinguacousy Rd", match the real storefront.

How the store works: a collection time is given for a repair and the phone is tried at the counter; the store handles number transfers and the old plan then closes by itself; trade-ins are taken; the store looks up the address and books the Bell technician for home services; the store carries iPhone and Android phones; a plan can be set up on a phone the customer already owns; a customer who rings first is told whether a model or colour is in stock; the store goes through offers, plans and home-service choices with a customer who brings a recent bill; walk-ins need no appointment and a booked visit means the store expects them; form requests get a call back; Ali can be named on the Visit page.

What to bring: the pages say photo ID in case it is needed, a recent bill showing the account number when moving a number, the address and unit number for home internet and TV, and the phone for a repair.

Program details to double-check: read on Bell and third-party pages on October 26 and 27, 2026: Member Benefits perks change over time; select on-demand movies and series from the Fibe TV app can be downloaded to a phone or tablet (Bell says watching recordings needs a PVR); Lucky Mobile has no credit check, no lock-in and no overage charges for data; Bell says people who already have Virgin Plus home internet or TV keep their plan, price and equipment; whether a Home Phone line can be had without internet or TV is unconfirmed (the pages say it depends on the address); Bell SmartPay (eligible 2-year plan, credit approval, rest of the price due if the plan ends early) and Device Return Option terms come from Bell's support pages, and trade press now calls the Device Return Option Flex Option, so the pages use both names and say details depend on the plan.

Dated notices: Virgin Plus prepaid plans end on January 15, 2027, so take that notice off after the date; re-check the Virgin Plus home internet and TV change (from January 14, 2026) if Virgin Plus changes it.

Carrier logos: get sign-off from the Bell dealer or brand contact before showing the Bell, Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile logos online (Bell's logo standards ask for clear space equal to the width of the two Ls and list info.branding@bell.ca for questions).

Privacy page: confirm that the site sets no tracking cookies, that form requests reach the store through the host's form service, that requests the store no longer needs are deleted, and that the map loads from Google only when a visitor presses Show the map.

Where the forms go: the repair and visit forms deliver nothing until the site is on a host that can receive them (Netlify form detection, or a form service such as Formspree); send one real test request before launch.

"Authorised" or "Authorized": the card and the brief say Bell Authorised Retailer and the site uses that spelling, but the Bell decals in the shop window (Google listing photos) say Authorized Retailer; use what the dealer agreement requires.
Google rating: 4.1 from 95 reviews on October 27, 2026: refresh it, or remove it from the home page; it links to the store's Google reviews, which include some complaints.
Design 1 photographs (optional): design 1 uses drawings; real photos of the shop front, counter and team could sit next to them.

Design 2 photographs: eleven of the twelve photos are stock photos (the twelfth is the AI-generated home page image, next item); four show recognisable people (family-tv, video-call, cafe-business, seniors-phone) with no model release on record (family-tv was uploaded by the World Sikh Organization of Canada); the same few photos repeat across pages; swap them for the store's own photos to remove that risk.

Design 2 home page photo: the hero image (a hand holding a small folding phone) is AI-generated and was supplied for the preview; the tool and its terms are not known, it is not a photo of a real device, and its screen shows Apple's app icons and logo; confirm the tool's terms allow commercial use and deal with the Apple icons, or replace it with a licensed photo, before design 2 goes live.
Design 3 photographs: stock photos of hands, rooms and parts, none showing a recognisable person or the store; real photos of the counter and repair bench would suit it best.
Design 3 wordmark: approve the champagne-gold version of the T Wireless logo (a soft gradient from light champagne to bronze, not the red original), or ask for the red logo on a pearl plate.
